# Adam Hickey

> Senior product designer in Minneapolis, Minnesota, with twenty years across visual design, interactive experiences and enterprise software. He brings visual intelligence to digital products and understands what it takes to make them work: complicated interfaces made clear, a visual hierarchy that holds across hundreds of screens, brand personality carried into an interface without costing it clarity, and the details fixed until the software feels finished. Eight years as a graphic designer and hybrid interactive designer and developer at three Minneapolis studios (ByDesign, LEVEL, Pixel Farm), thirteen years designing enterprise applications and design systems at RBA, and products of his own since, designed and built end to end. Open to a senior hands-on product design role: in-house, remote or hybrid in the Twin Cities, with a team that can hire in Minnesota.

Contact: adam@adamhickey.com. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/adamdhickey/

Every page is plain HTML with its content in the markup; nothing is rendered by script. Each page carries a canonical URL, an Open Graph card and a schema.org graph (Person, ProfessionalService, WebSite, WebPage, Article, BreadcrumbList), and https://adamhickey.com/sitemap.xml lists all forty-two pages with a last-modified date.

## What I bring

Four things, each shown in the work below, in one band of the homepage (https://adamhickey.com/#problems):

- Make complexity clear: difficult workflows and dense information turned into interfaces people can read at the speed they work. Shown in the SAP suite, the dispatch cockpit and the grant platform.
- Establish visual coherence: type, color, hierarchy, spacing and reusable systems, so a large set of screens reads as one product. Shown in the SAP design system, Innovators Studio and this site.
- Connect visual identity and user experience: a recognizable personality carried into the interface without costing it clarity. Shown in Door County Found, Lucy Learns and Say When.
- Bring the details to life: prototyping, interaction design, front-end knowledge and visual judgment, until it feels finished. Shown in the studio years, Agent Review and Faunaform.

## Selected work

- [Making 40+ enterprise apps feel like one product](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/sap-product-maturity.html): lead UX for a global corporation's SAP Fiori suite: one visual language, one hierarchy and one accessibility standard across 40+ apps built by many teams, with design-to-development time down about a third and production UI defects roughly halved while the program ran, and how each was counted.
- [An identity that made a global innovation network feel like one place](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/innovators-studio-visual-identity.html): a mark, an illustration and badge system, communication templates and a community platform for a corporation's intrapreneurs, over four fiscal years, with a marketing manager and a production designer.
- [Dog training you can follow with a leash in one hand](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/lucy-learns.html): Lucy Learns, an illustrated, installable app for his own household: one instruction a screen, type you can read from a step away, progress in the trainer's own levels, and the voice-command version the dog heard as cues for her, which came out after real sessions. The teleprompter that would replace the timer is a concept, not built. The app is live at https://adamdhickey-collab.github.io/lucy-learns/.
- [A travel guide that feels like advice from someone who knows the place](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/door-county-found.html): Door County Found, an editorial travel brand in cream, harbor navy and beacon gold, a rule that real places get real photographs, a writing system, and a working site his sister keeps current through a web form. Live at https://doorcountyfound.com.
- [Eight years of brand-led sites, campaigns and apps at three Minneapolis studios](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/hybrid-designer.html): the studio years, 2005 to 2013, as an interactive designer and developer: Lund Boats, Fulton Beer, Hazelden, Northern Spark, Dorsey & Whitney, Feed Friendsy and the Learn to Live identity, designed and built.
- [Say When: a coffee brand built on three plain words](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/say-when.html): a self-initiated, fictional brand concept with no client, no research study and nothing for sale, labeled so wherever it appears: strategy, naming, identity, packaging, a campaign and a working storefront prototype at https://adamhickey.com/say-when/index.html.

Also reachable, off the homepage's first screen:

- [Grant tools unified into one trusted platform](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/usda-operational-overhead.html): lead product design for the USDA-backed Nutrition Incentive Hub: complex grant information laid out so people could read it and trust it, and a 45-to-55-hour process down to just over ten.
- [One real-time view of a 450+ truck fleet](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/dispatch-complexity.html): lead product design for Midwest Couriers: a cockpit dense enough for expert dispatchers and clear enough to read at their speed.
- [13 years designing enterprise software](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/enterprise-consulting.html): the RBA years, 2013 to 2026, for CBRE, Toro, Banner Bank and International Trucks.
- [How I'm building Faunaform](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/faunaform.html): a screen-print studio for Minnesota wildlife art, in progress: seven animals, each drawn for one hour of one day, to be printed by hand in four flat inks. An image model draws from written briefs, software built with coding agents makes every drawing printable, and every call about the art is his. Nothing is printed yet, and the page says which pictures are simulations.
- [How I built While We're Here](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/while-were-here.html): a 300mm square hardcover of essays, designed spread by spread and produced from HTML and CSS through a paged-media engine.
- [How I built this site](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/this-site.html): forty-two pages of plain HTML with no framework and no build step, three token files under four normative specs, and eleven checks that measure the rendered page before anything ships.
- [Other things I make](https://adamhickey.com/other.html): the book, and identity and illustration work for clients.

## Experiments

Self-directed work, labeled as such. The index is at https://adamhickey.com/lab/index.html.

- [Agent Review: where design judgment goes when coding agents join the team](https://adamhickey.com/lab/agent-review.html): a case study with a working React prototype and a public Storybook, following one feature in a made-up product called Relay through six stages, each saying what the designer does and what the coding agent does. Everything in its scenarios is simulated and labeled so, and none of it has been tested with users. The prototype is at https://adamdhickey-collab.github.io/agent-review/, the Storybook at https://adamdhickey-collab.github.io/agent-review/storybook/, and the source at https://github.com/adamdhickey-collab/agent-review.
- [Dispatch Cockpit: an AI recommendation the dispatcher can check and overrule](https://adamhickey.com/prototype/dispatch-cockpit.html): human-in-the-loop decision support for freight dispatch on synthetic data: the factors weighed with their values and ages, a close call that names its tradeoff, a federal hours-of-service limit enforced before anything is scored, and a one-click override that asks why afterwards. Informed by the Midwest Couriers work; every figure invented, not tested with dispatchers.
- [The Say When storefront](https://adamhickey.com/say-when/index.html): the coffee concept's shop as a working prototype: a three-question finder that says why it picked, a cart in the browser, and a checkout that says it is pretend on every line.
- [Designing motion with Claude Code](https://adamhickey.com/lab/designing-motion.html): an exploration of motion and interaction: a three-step scroll story drawn as one anime.js timeline whose playhead is the scroll position. Reduced motion jumps between finished states; without JavaScript the finished drawing stays.

## Writing

Ten articles on product design, design systems and working with coding agents: one to start with, then nine in three collections, the system, the build and the judgment. Each answers in its first paragraph a question people ask before they know who to ask. The index is at https://adamhickey.com/writing/index.html.

Start here:

- [What makes a good product designer now?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-makes-a-good-product-designer-now.html): coding agents made building fast, so a bad decision travels further and the designer's work moved to what the building is made from: a design system that says what each part means, building to find out rather than to produce more, and a clear line between what software does alone and what a person decides. Told through Agent Review's quiet cancel link and Lucy Learns's three tries.

The system:

- [What changes when AI agents join the product team?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-changes-when-ai-agents-join-the-product-team.html): the design system stops being a library people consult and becomes the instructions a builder follows, and an agent cannot ask what you meant. Credited to Netflix's design system team, worked through Agent Review and the SAP program.
- [What a design system needs to explain to an agent](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-a-design-system-needs-to-explain-to-an-agent.html): components and tokens tell a coding agent what to build with; it also needs what each part means, how it behaves, where the usual answer holds and where it does not.
- [What does a design system need once AI is in the product?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-does-a-design-system-need-once-ai-is-in-the-product.html): six things a system built for facts needs once AI hands it claims, starting with a slot for a value's source and age.

The build:

- [What is a product designer for, when anyone can build?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-is-a-product-designer-for-when-anyone-can-build.html): understanding why something matters, making it real fast enough to find out, and knowing when it isn't good enough. Worked through Door County Found and Faunaform.
- [What should a working prototype actually prove?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-should-a-working-prototype-actually-prove.html): whether the idea is worth building, in real code on real inputs with the people who would use it, ending in a build, kill, or park call.
- [How should you test a product now that AI can help?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/how-should-you-test-a-product-now-that-ai-can-help.html): let agents find what's broken, let people show you what they misunderstand, and let the numbers say how often. Worked through Lucy Learns and Agent Review.

The judgment:

- [Who decides when software can act on its own?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/who-decides-when-software-can-act-on-its-own.html): the person accountable for the outcome, and the design work is making sure they really can. Worked through Dispatch Cockpit.
- [Enterprise AI should help people decide, not just answer](https://adamhickey.com/writing/enterprise-ai-should-help-people-decide-not-just-answer.html): the evidence beside the recommendation, calibrated rather than maximal trust, and the decision rather than the acceptance rate as the measure.
- [What does a person need to supervise an AI agent?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-does-a-person-need-to-supervise-an-ai-agent.html): the line between what an agent does alone and what it asks about, an approval that carries its evidence, a record the run can be reconstructed from, and three kinds of stop.

Five more articles keep their addresses but are no longer on the index:

- [What makes an interface feel finished?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-makes-an-interface-feel-finished.html): type on a scale, color as a measured pair, motion as a duration and a curve, a decision for every state, spacing from tokens, and the checks that hold all of it; craft as a list you can name and measure.
- [What does a product design engineer actually do?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-does-a-product-design-engineer-actually-do.html): the component as the deliverable, tokens that flow one way, pull requests as design reviews, prototypes on a branch, and the checks that hold the system.
- [What does a developer need from an interface on a bad day?](https://adamhickey.com/writing/what-does-a-developer-need-from-an-interface-on-a-bad-day.html): the screens a developer opens most are the ones that open when something broke, so the error message, the empty state and the log are the product.
- [Designing for the moment the workflow breaks](https://adamhickey.com/writing/designing-for-the-moment-the-workflow-breaks.html): what an operational user needs when an order stalls, followed through one illustrative order.
- [What I learned standardizing UX across 40+ SAP Fiori apps](https://adamhickey.com/writing/standardizing-ux-across-40-sap-fiori-apps.html): one style guide and component library, feedback loops, checks in the release process, and teams that own it, with how each figure was counted and what it cannot show.

## Optional

- [Homepage](https://adamhickey.com/): the person, six selected projects, the four things he brings to a team, the experiments, and About, which tells the career as one story: graphic design and interactive work first, then enterprise product design, then both at once.
- [Design system](https://adamhickey.com/design-system/index.html): the tokens, type, spacing, corners, motion and components behind the site, every value read live from the stylesheets, the eleven checks that hold every page to it, and a tokens.json export in the W3C format.
